definitions.explanation: Something personally experienced or undergone, as opposed to learned secondhand. Emphasizes direct, personal involvement in an event or activity.

examples.japanese: {貴重|きちょう}な{体験|たいけん}だった。
{海外|かいがい}で{働|はたら}く{体験|たいけん}をした。
examples.english: I had the experience of working abroad.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもたちに{自然|しぜん}の{中|なか}での{体験|たいけん}{学習|がくしゅう}をさせたい。
examples.english: I want to give the children hands-on learning experiences in nature.

notes:
GRAMMAR: Functions as a noun and as a する verb ({体験|たいけん}する).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {体験|たいけん}{談|だん} (personal account, firsthand story)
- {体験|たいけん}{学習|がくしゅう} (experiential learning)
- {体験|たいけん}{入学|にゅうがく} (trial enrollment)
- {無料|むりょう}{体験|たいけん} (free trial)
- {体験|たいけん}レッスン (trial lesson)

SIMILAR WORDS: {経験|けいけん} also means "experience" but is broader and more general. {体験|たいけん} emphasizes direct, firsthand, often one-time personal involvement, while {経験|けいけん} includes accumulated knowledge and skill from past events.
